lesson.title: Serve Away From the Lean
lesson.hook: The returner leans to cover one serve. The lean tells you where to serve.
lesson.memHTML: Read the lean. Serve away from it.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you serve, glance at where the returner is standing before you toss.

pro.label: Serving to the forehand corner
pro.moment: ATP players win 51 per cent of second-serve points served to the forehand corner and 49 per cent to the backhand corner. On the deuce side, well-placed second serves to the forehand corner win 8.5 per cent more points than well-placed serves to the backhand.
pro.read: The corner they protect isn't always the one to serve at.
pro.src: ATP Tour, Golden Set Analytics for Tennis Data Innovations (Dec 2022)

drill.name: Serve away from the lean
drill.how: The returner takes a clear lean before each serve, wide or toward the T. Serve away from it. Score a point for every return they only block or don't reach; then let them lean late and see if you still read it.

lesson.cue: Read the lean. Serve away from it.

steps.name: They lean toward the T
steps.sit: First serve from the deuce side. The returner has moved toward the T to protect their backhand.
steps.q: Which first serve makes their return hardest?
steps.payoff: Leaning toward the T leaves the wide serve too far away.
steps.principle: Where they lean is where they're ready. Serve to the side they left.
steps.why: They read your serve a quarter of a second after you hit it, then have to get beside the ball. Out wide is the furthest from where they're leaning, and they can't get there.
steps.take: Returner leaning one way? Serve the other.

lines.A: Right: they're leaning toward the T, and wide is out of reach. An ace.
lines.B: Down the T is where they're leaning: they're in time.
lines.C: At the body they just step aside: set, they attack, and you're stretched.
lines.D: Slower at the body gives them even longer: they attack, and you're stretched.

steps.name: Now they shade wide
steps.sit: After that ace they've shaded wide to stop it happening again.
steps.payoff: They covered the wide serve, so the T is now the long way round.
steps.principle: The lean moves, so the target moves.
steps.why: Shading wide takes away the ace, but it opens the T. They can only block it, and the slow return gives you time on your next ball.
steps.take: They moved to stop it? Serve where they moved from.

lines.A: At the body they just step aside: set, they attack, and you're stretched.
lines.B: Slower, out wide, into their lean: they attack, and you're stretched.
lines.C: Right: they shaded wide, so the T rushes them. Blocked; you're set early.
lines.D: Wide is exactly what they're covering now: they're in time.

steps.name: Ad side, protecting the backhand
steps.sit: Now the ad side. This returner stands wide to protect their backhand.
steps.q: Which first serve makes their return hardest?
steps.payoff: Away from the lean beats aiming at the weaker wing.
steps.principle: Serve the space they gave up, even if it's their forehand.
steps.why: Out wide goes to their backhand, but that's the side they're protecting. Down the T reaches their forehand, but it's the long way from where they stand, and they can only block it.
steps.take: Protecting the backhand? The T to the forehand is open.

lines.A: Slower, to the backhand they're protecting: they attack, and you're stretched.
lines.B: Right: the T, away from the lean. Blocked; you're set early.
lines.C: Out wide to the backhand is what they're covering: they're in time.
lines.D: At the body they just step aside: set, they attack, and you're stretched.
